- Model tends to overestimate prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, showing a persistent lag in capturing downward momentum.
- Overreacts to short-term volatility, overshooting after sharp price increases.
- Fails to account for mean reversion in the final 10–15 days, leading to sustained overestimation.
- Forecasts are generally too optimistic in the first 5–7 days, then gradually adjust but still lag behind true values.
- Model exhibits a consistent bias toward higher prices in the middle of the forecast, especially when historical prices are trending upward.
